mistakes.why: The derivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> is 1: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx} = 1 + 2e^x = 3</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

The equation is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y - x</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x - y</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3 - 0 = 3</annotation></semantics></math>.

For the curve <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = x + 1 + 2e^x</annotation></semantics></math>, find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = x^2</annotation></semantics></math> a solution to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\frac{dy}{dx} = 2y</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x > 0</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: Yes: at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 1</annotation></semantics></math> both sides equal 2.
No: an <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> on the left side is not allowed.

items.q: Which differential equation does <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \sin(2x)</annotation></semantics></math> satisfy?

For which positive constant <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> does <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = e^{kx}</annotation></semantics></math> satisfy <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">″</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y'' - y' - 6y = 0</annotation></semantics></math>?

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k = -2</annotation></semantics></math> also solves <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>k</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k^2 - k - 6 = 0</annotation></semantics></math>, but the question asks for the positive value.

Substitute: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>k</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k^2e^{kx} - ke^{kx} - 6e^{kx}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 0</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>k</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k^2 - k - 6 = 0</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k = 3</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \frac{1}{x}</annotation></semantics></math> satisfies <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx} = -y^2</annotation></semantics></math> wherever it is defined. items.q: Let <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.2</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 5e^{-0.2t}</annotation></semantics></math>. mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.2</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dt} = -e^{-0.2t}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.2</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5e^{-0.2t}</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.2</mn><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dt} = -0.2y</annotation></semantics></math>; the 5 is already inside <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>.
The exponent is negative, so the derivative carries a minus sign.

The field is drawn for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx} = 2x - y</annotation></semantics></math>. mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x + y</annotation></semantics></math>. The equation subtracts <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2(1) - 3 = -1</annotation></semantics></math>.

The 2 multiplies <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2(1) - 3 = -1</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 - 3</annotation></semantics></math>.

Along the vertical line <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, how do the slopes of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx} = 2x - y</annotation></semantics></math> change as <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> increases?

Which describes the segment at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(-1, 0)</annotation></semantics></math> in the field of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx} = 2x - y</annotation></semantics></math>?

items.q: Find the slope at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(-1, 1)</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx} = x^2(y - 2)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That uses <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> instead of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(-1)^2 = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, so the slope is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 \cdot (1 - 2) = -1</annotation></semantics></math>.

The second factor uses <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y - 2 = 1 - 2 = -1</annotation></semantics></math>, so the slope is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(-1)^2 \cdot (-1) = -1</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find the slope at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1, 3)</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx} = x^2(y - 2)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y - 2 = 3 - 2 = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, positive.

options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln|y| = -x^2 + C</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Why may the constant <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math> in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>A</mi><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = Ae^{-x^2}</annotation></semantics></math> be negative, as for the lowest curve?
options: Because <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{-x^2}</annotation></semantics></math> can be negative.

Because <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math> can be negative, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>C</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{C}</annotation></semantics></math> can be negative.

From <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln|y| = -x^2 + C</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">±</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>C</mi></msup><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \pm e^{C}e^{-x^2}</annotation></semantics></math>; <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">±</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>C</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A = \pm e^{C}</annotation></semantics></math> takes either sign.
It may not: negative curves do not satisfy the equation.

items.q: The top curve is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 2e^{-x^2}</annotation></semantics></math>. Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: The exponent is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-x^2 = -1</annotation></semantics></math>, so the value is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mi>e</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2e^{-1} = \frac{2}{e}</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> is not 1: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(1) = 2e^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: The <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>-axis, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 0</annotation></semantics></math>, also satisfies <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx} = -2xy</annotation></semantics></math>. What happened to it during separation?
options: Dividing by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> assumed <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y \ne 0</annotation></semantics></math>; the family <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>A</mi><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = Ae^{-x^2}</annotation></semantics></math> recovers it with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A = 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

It is not a solution, since <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln 0</annotation></semantics></math> is undefined.

It is the curve with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C = 0</annotation></semantics></math> in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln|y| = -x^2 + C</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Which is a correct first step in separating <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>y</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{x^2}{y}</annotation></semantics></math>?

A separation ends with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln|y| = 2x + 5</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y > 0</annotation></semantics></math>. Solve for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: Exponentiate the whole right side: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mn>5</mn></msup><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = e^{2x + 5} = e^5e^{2x}</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{2x} + 5</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln y = 2x + 5</annotation></semantics></math> means <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = e^{2x + 5}</annotation></semantics></math>; undo the logarithm.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>a</mi></msup><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>b</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{a + b} = e^{a}e^{b}</annotation></semantics></math>, a product, not a sum.

items.q: Separate and integrate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mi>y</mi><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx} = y\cos x</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln|y| = \sin x + C</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln|y| = -\sin x + C</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln|y| = \sin x</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: A student writes: "<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx} = x + y</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mi>y</mi></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{y} = x\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>." What is wrong?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x + y</annotation></semantics></math> is a sum, so dividing by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> leaves <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mi>y</mi></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{x}{y} + 1</annotation></semantics></math>: the equation is not separable.

Nothing: dividing by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> is allowed when <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y \ne 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

The student should have written <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y\,dy = x\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>.
The student forgot <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ C</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Separate and integrate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>T</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.05</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>20</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dT}{dt} = -0.05(T - 20)</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.05</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln|T| - 20 = -0.05t + C</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>20</mn><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.05</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln|T - 20| = -0.05t</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>20</mn><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.05</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln|T - 20| = -0.05t + C</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: After separating, a student writes <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln|y| + C_1 = x^3 + C_2</annotation></semantics></math>. Why is it enough to write a single <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ C</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: Because the two constants are equal and cancel.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_2 - C_1</annotation></semantics></math> is just another constant, so one <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math> on one side covers every case.
Because the constant is added at the end, after solving.

items.q: Separating <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mi>y</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{x}{y}</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y^2 = x^2 + C</annotation></semantics></math>. Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math> for the solution curve through <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1, 3)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: Square the coordinates: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>9</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9 = 1 + C</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C = y^2 - x^2 = 9 - 1</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>9</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9 + 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>9</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9 = 1 + C</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C = +8</annotation></semantics></math>.
